The dominant theme: the PR is titled "enhance … validation," but its net effect on validation is **subtractive** — `skip_validations` on both create and revise paths, plus a total sanitization bypass (`post.rb:133`) feeding attacker-controlled HTML from an RSS feed straight into `cooked`. The `poll_feed.rb:35` → `topic_embed.rb:13` → `best.html.erb:19` chain is the one I'd block on.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:133 — CRITICAL: `return raw if cook_method == raw_html` makes cooked a byte copy of raw, skipping PrettyText sanitize AND Plugin::Filter :after_post_cook; every XSS below funnels through this line

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` with a `:raw_html` option and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The new feed/import path (`TopicEmbed.import` and `Jobs::PollFeed`) sets `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and passes HTML content from RSS/remote pages (only `scrub`/`CGI.unescapeHTML`, and Readability tag/attribute selection—not PrettyText sanitization). Since views (e.g., `embed/best.html.erb`) render `raw post.cooked`, this introduces a verifiable XSS risk: imported/embedded content can bypass PrettyText sanitization and plugin filters by design through this new early return.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — CRITICAL: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content) turns a feed's correctly-escaped <script> into live <script>, then stores it with NO sanitizer (Readability's allowlist only guards the import_remote path)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed item body is set as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed into `TopicEmbed.import`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any HTML in the feed becomes executable markup. Therefore, decoding entities with `CGI.unescapeHTML` can turn `<script>` into a real `<script>` tag that will be stored and rendered without sanitization. The finding correctly identifies a verifiable XSS risk on the feed-import path (unlike `import_remote`, which uses Readability allowlists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — HIGH: url interpolated unescaped into <a href='#{url}'>; a feed link `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)` passes the line-11 regex and breaks out of the attribute (I18n %{link} does not escape)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows URLs containing single quotes and event handlers (e.g., `http://x/' onmouseover='alert(1)`). That `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The post is created with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so there is no escaping/sanitization barrier in this code path. This is a verifiable XSS injection introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 — HIGH: `raw post.cooked` renders unsanitized HTML on the Discourse origin; layout sets no iframe sandbox and no CSP, and the same cooked value is served in the main topic view

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` (`:raw_html`) in `Post#cook` that returns `raw` directly, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` using `contents` pulled from RSS/remote pages (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and `Readability::Document#content`) and then stores that HTML as the post’s `raw`. In `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, the embed view renders that value with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which for these imported posts is the unsanitized HTML. This is a verifiable XSS risk introduced by the diff; the layout shown also does not add iframe sandboxing or CSP defenses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48-50 — HIGH: Readability `attributes: %w[href src]` allowlists by NAME with no scheme check, so `<a href="javascript:...">` survives (onerror= is stripped; the javascript: hole is live)

app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — HIGH: SSRF w/ exfiltration — open(url).read on unauthenticated params[:embed_url]; invalid_host? checks only the PRE-redirect URL and open-uri follows redirects unchecked; body is then published as a public topic

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which does `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). This is invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` using `@embed_url` ultimately sourced from the unauthenticated `params[:embed_url]` in `EmbedController#best` (it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` with that URL when no embed exists). `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` only validates the host of the *original* URL string (`URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`) before calling `import_remote`, but `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default. That means an attacker can supply an embed URL on the allowed host that 30x-redirects to an internal resource (e.g., 169.254.169.254 or localhost), and the response body is then imported into a post via `TopicEmbed.import`, effectively exfiltrating fetched content into a public topic. The redirect target host is never re-validated, so the SSRF vector is real in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — HIGH: bare Kernel#open on unvalidated feed_polling_url (free-form setting, no validator) — a leading `|` executes a shell command; `/etc/passwd` or file:// yields local file read imported into a public topic
matched_golden_ids: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root problem: PollFeed uses Kernel#open on a free-form, unvalidated `feed_polling_url`, enabling an attacker who can control that setting to make the server open arbitrary resources. While the candidate emphasizes additional open-uri vectors (pipe command execution, local file/file:// reads), it still covers the golden issue’s SSRF/arbitrary URL fetch risk from unvalidated input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — MEDIUM: t[:link] from an attacker-supplied XML export reaches Kernel#open with no TopicRetriever host check

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path was changed from creating a post with the permalink to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (no allowlist/host validation) and there is no `TopicRetriever`-style `embeddable_host` check in this code path. Since `t[:link]` comes from the parsed Disqus export, a crafted/untrusted export could cause the importer to fetch arbitrary URLs (SSRF/unintended network access) and potentially hit `Kernel#open` behaviors. This is a concrete issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — MEDIUM: the ONLY gate in front of the SSRF sink, job-enqueue sink and raw-HTML render is a spoofable Referer header; scheme/port blind

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 — MEDIUM: unauthenticated enqueue with no RateLimiter; the throttle key is the FULL url, so ?cachebust=N defeats it — unbounded queue + Redis growth, one outbound fetch per request

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url) for any request that passes ensure_embeddable (which only checks Referer host and can be spoofed by a direct HTTP client). The only throttling is inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? using a Redis key derived from the full @embed_url ("retrieved:#{@embed_url}") with a 60s TTL. Because the key includes the entire URL, changing the query string (e.g., ?cachebust=N) produces a new Redis key, bypasses the throttle, and also bypasses the existence check since TopicEmbed is keyed by exact embed_url. This allows an attacker to enqueue arbitrarily many jobs and trigger an outbound fetch per distinct URL variant. Redis key growth is time-bounded by TTL but can still spike under load; the Sidekiq queue growth is unbounded at enqueue time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:9 — MEDIUM: unconditional 30s reload re-enters #best and enqueues another job; if retrieval can never succeed (embed_by_username unset, remote 404) the loop never terminates

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` a `setTimeout` unconditionally reloads the page every 30s. On each reload it hits `EmbedController#best`, and when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is still nil it always executes `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` again. There is no termination condition in the view/controller for cases where retrieval will never succeed (e.g., `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` blank causing `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to return without importing, or repeated remote fetch failures). Although `TopicRetriever` throttles actual retrieval (`retrieved_recently?`), the controller still enqueues a new job on every reload, leading to an infinite reload loop and repeated job enqueues when the embed never becomes available.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — MEDIUM: no open/read timeout and no size cap; RetrieveTopic lacks retry:false, so a slowloris pins a Sidekiq thread

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) without any explicit `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` or response size cap, so a slow or never-ending response can block the executing thread. That path is reachable from the `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` Sidekiq job via `TopicRetriever#fetch_http -> TopicEmbed.import_remote`. Unlike `Jobs::PollFeed` (which sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`), `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` has no `sidekiq_options`, so it will use Sidekiq’s default retry behavior, potentially re-running a blocking fetch repeatedly and tying up worker threads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_creator.rb:216 — MEDIUM: plumbs cook_method through PostCreator's unfiltered @opts hash with no allowlist, creating a sanitization-bypass switch for any caller that forwards user params

lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — MEDIUM: caller-controlled validation bypass on the shared edit path; save's return value is discarded, so a failed write is silent while update_column still records the content as imported
app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:28 — LOW: "ALLOWALL" is not a valid X-Frame-Options token; UAs ignoring it apply no framing policy, and the intent is never expressed to the browser

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable the code sets `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"`. X-Frame-Options only defines `DENY`, `SAMEORIGIN`, and (deprecated) `ALLOW-FROM <uri>`; `ALLOWALL` is not a valid token. As a result, user agents that enforce XFO will typically ignore the header value (treating it as if no XFO policy were set), so this header does not reliably express the intended framing behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 — LOW (corrected, not XSS): html_escape does not escape `\`, so a Referer ending in `\` produces a JS SyntaxError killing the resize handshake; targetOrigin is also the client-supplied full URL rather than a server-derived origin

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — LOW: ?embed_url[]=x enqueues an Array; URI() raises ArgumentError, which the `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` does not catch

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbedController#best` does `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` and then enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. In Rails, a request like `?embed_url[]=x` makes `params[:embed_url]` an Array, and `require(:embed_url)` will return that Array (it does not enforce scalar type). The job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) passes `args[:embed_url]` into `TopicRetriever.new(...)`, and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` calls `URI(@embed_url).host` rescuing only `URI::InvalidURIError`. If `@embed_url` is an Array, `URI(...)` raises a non-`URI::InvalidURIError` (typically `TypeError`), which is not rescued, causing the job to crash. The finding’s file/exception class is slightly off (the `URI()` call is in `TopicRetriever`, and it’s more likely `TypeError` than `ArgumentError`), but the underlying defect is real and introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 — LOW (unverified): discourse_expires_in on a body containing request.referer and a current_user-scoped TopicView, with no Vary; cache semantics not confirmable in this checkout

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` has a stray trailing `if`; hard SyntaxError under plain ERB, and under Erubis it parses as a modifier-if whose condition is the NEXT buffer append — renders today only by luck and emits whitespace out of order

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 — i.content is nil on RSS 2.0 (simple-rss 1.3.1 method_missing is a bare Hash lookup; RSS exposes description/content_encoded). i.id at :33 is Atom-only. Despite the "RSS/ATOM" setting text, only Atom works

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — open(url).read with no `require 'open-uri'` in this file; ruby-readability does not pull it in, so in non-eager-loading envs Kernel#open hits Errno::ENOENT

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` but the file only `require`s `nokogiri` and `ruby-readability`; it never `require 'open-uri'`. In Ruby, URL support for `Kernel#open` is provided by `open-uri`, otherwise `open("http://...")` is treated as a filesystem path and can raise `Errno::ENOENT`. The diff shows other code (`poll_feed.rb`) explicitly requiring `open-uri`, reinforcing that it’s not assumed globally. So this is a concrete missing-require defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:4 + app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1 — neither asset is added to config.assets.precompile (untouched by this PR) and production sets compile=false ⇒ AssetNotPrecompiled / 404

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new assets `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and the new layout references the stylesheet via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`. However, the diff does not show the app’s asset precompile configuration (e.g., `config/initializers/assets.rb` or any Discourse-specific asset build/precompile setup), nor does it show whether these assets are already covered by a wildcard precompile rule or included via an existing manifest. The claim that production has `compile=false` and that these assets are not precompiled is therefore not verifiable from this diff alone and depends on code/config not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:24 — `if post.present?` is the wrong liveness check: PostCreator#create returns @post even after ActiveRecord::Rollback (raised at :59, before save_post), so create! runs with nil topic_id/post_id against NOT NULL columns. Should be persisted?

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` doing `post = creator.create` and then `TopicEmbed.create!` only when `post.present?`. While it’s true that `present?` does not guarantee the record is persisted, the finding’s core claim (that `PostCreator#create` returns `@post` even after an `ActiveRecord::Rollback` at specific lines) is not verifiable from this diff: the `PostCreator#create` implementation and any rollback behavior are not included here. Without evidence in the diff that `creator.create` can yield a non-persisted `Post` object, the assertion that `create!` will run with nil `topic_id/post_id` is speculative rather than a demonstrable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:21 — wrapping PostCreator in an outer Topic.transaction makes its inner Post.transaction savepoint-less, so its ActiveRecord::Rollback is swallowed without rolling back; needs requires_new: true

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.import` wrapping `PostCreator.new(...).create` in a `Topic.transaction`, but there is no evidence in this diff that `PostCreator#create` opens its own `Post.transaction` or raises `ActiveRecord::Rollback`. The finding relies on unseen implementation details. Also, in Rails, a nested transaction without `requires_new` joins the outer transaction; an `ActiveRecord::Rollback` raised inside it does not get “swallowed without rolling back” — it marks the surrounding transaction for rollback (it’s not an inner independent rollback unless a savepoint/`requires_new` is used). So the described defect is not verifiable from the diff and is likely a mischaracterization of Rails transaction behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15,25 — check-then-insert against the UNIQUE index is a TOCTOU race; the loser raises unhandled RecordNotUnique and aborts the whole rss.items.each loop

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!` inside a transaction. Since `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a UNIQUE index (migration adds `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), two concurrent imports of the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then race to insert; the loser will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or equivalent). There is no rescue/handling in `import` or in the caller `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`’s `rss.items.each` loop, so the exception would bubble up and terminate the loop/job early.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:31-38 — update branch has no transaction (unlike the create branch); if update_column fails after revise!, the stale sha1 causes a new post revision every hour forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the create path wraps post+embed creation in a `Topic.transaction`, but the update path does `revisor.revise!(...)` and then separately `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` with no transaction. That means a partial success is possible: the post revision can be persisted (via `PostRevisor` saving the post) but if `update_column` raises/fails afterward (DB error, connection drop, etc.), `embed.content_sha1` remains stale. On the next poll/retrieval, `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` will still be true, causing another unnecessary revision attempt. The “forever” phrasing is a bit strong (it would repeat until the sha1 update succeeds), but the underlying atomicity/correctness problem is real and visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — protocol-relative URLs are corrupted: `//cdn.example.com/a.png` → `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png` (verified)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, both link and image URLs are rewritten whenever href/src starts_with?('/'). This also matches protocol-relative URLs like "//cdn.example.com/a.png". The code then strips all leading slashes via sub(/^\/+/, '') and prefixes with "#{prefix}/", producing "http://<embed_host>/cdn.example.com/a.png" instead of preserving the intended protocol-relative CDN URL. This is directly verifiable from the rewrite logic in app/models/topic_embed.rb.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:64 — relative URLs without a leading slash (`images/x.png`, `../foo`) are left untouched and resolve against the Discourse host; the :55 comment "Convert any relative URLs to absolute" overclaims

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` (commented “Convert any relative URLs to absolute”), the code only rewrites `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`. Other valid relative forms like `images/x.png`, `./foo`, `../foo`, or protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn...`) are not converted. Those will therefore remain relative in the stored raw HTML and will resolve relative to the Discourse page URL/host when rendered, not the source site, contradicting the comment and causing broken links/images for such feeds/pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:57 — URI(url) unguarded; `http://exa mple.com/x` passes the :11 regex then raises URI::InvalidURIError out of import, killing the remaining feed items (verified)

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: TopicEmbed.import only checks `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which allows invalid URLs containing spaces (e.g. `http://exa mple.com/x`). That URL is then passed to `absolutize_urls`, which calls `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue. `URI()` will raise `URI::InvalidURIError`, and PollFeed’s `rss.items.each` loop does not rescue per-item, so one bad URL can abort the job and prevent remaining feed items from importing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — /^https?:\/\// uses `^` (line anchor, not \A): "evil\nhttp://x.com" matches at offset 5 (verified); it also accepts bare "http://" with no host

app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place, and the appended footer comes from I18n, so content_sha1 is locale-dependent — changing default locale re-revises every imported post

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)}..."` mutates the caller-provided String in place, so the passed `contents` object is changed after the call. Also, `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)` is computed *after* appending a footer whose text comes from `I18n.t(...)`. That makes the stored SHA1 depend on the active locale/default locale at import time; if the locale used by the importer changes later, the same article body will produce a different SHA1 and will trigger the update/revise path (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`) for every already-imported URL, even when the upstream content is unchanged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:16 vs :22 — content_sha1 is hashed PRE-absolutize_urls while post.raw stores the POST-absolutize output, so the column is not a hash of what is actually stored
app/models/topic_embed.rb:37 — update_column bypasses updated_at, so the only per-row freshness signal for monitoring is dead

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes it runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`. In Rails, `update_column` skips validations/callbacks and does **not** touch timestamp columns, so `topic_embeds.updated_at` will not reflect that the row was updated even though the embed was refreshed. Since the table is created with `t.timestamps`, leaving `updated_at` stale is a verifiable behavioral issue introduced by this code path (freshness tracking via timestamps won’t work).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:32 — embed.post can be nil (post deleted); PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! then raises NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, immediately does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!(...)` with no nil-guard. Although `topic_embeds.post_id` is `null: false`, there is no foreign key or `dependent:` behavior shown, so if the referenced Post is deleted independently, `embed.post` will return `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will later crash (e.g., when it tries to access `@post`). This is a verifiable correctness issue in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15,79 — no URL canonicalization, so UNIQUE(embed_url) is not the real invariant; RSS links usually carry tracking params while embed.js sends the canonical URL, so PollFeed's topic is never matched and a duplicate is created

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed is keyed and looked up purely by the raw string `embed_url` (unique DB index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`, `topic_id_for_embed` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)`, and `TopicRetriever`/`EmbedController` pass the request param through unchanged). `Jobs::PollFeed` likewise imports using `i.link`/`i.id` without any normalization. There is no canonicalization/normalization step (e.g., stripping query params, normalizing trailing slashes, scheme, etc.), so the system will treat different URL representations of the same page as different embeds and create separate topics, and an embed request using a different form won’t match the topic created via the feed. The specific mention of tracking params vs canonical URL is an external scenario, but the underlying mismatch/duplication risk is directly implied by the exact-string uniqueness and lookups in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) runs a full hourly scheduled feed import synchronously inside a per-request job, concurrently with the real hourly run, under retry:false

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve, when feed polling is enabled it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` directly (synchronously) before doing the single-URL HTTP fetch. This is invoked from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (a regular Sidekiq job enqueued per embed request in EmbedController#best when no TopicEmbed exists), so embed traffic can trigger a full feed poll/import run. There is no locking around PollFeed, so it can run concurrently with the scheduled hourly PollFeed job, and it processes the entire feed (`rss.items.each`) rather than just the requested URL. This is a concrete performance/correctness risk introduced by the diff; the mention of `retry: false` is slightly misstated (it applies to the scheduled job, and direct invocation bypasses Sidekiq options), but the core issue is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — setnx + expire are non-atomic; a crash between them leaves a TTL-less key that permanently blocks that URL (nothing deletes it). Use SET k v NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then given a TTL via `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These are two separate Redis commands; if the process crashes or is interrupted after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will exist without an expiration and the method will subsequently treat it as “retrieved recently” forever (nothing in this code deletes that key). Using an atomic SET with NX+EX would avoid this failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 — host-equality only, no scheme check (ftp://host/x passes) and case-sensitive; www vs apex and any port/scheme variant silently 403

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, invalid_host? only checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` and does not restrict the URI scheme. As a result, an `embed_url` like `ftp://<embeddable_host>/x` will pass the host check and proceed to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which calls `open(url).read` (open-uri supports non-HTTP schemes such as ftp), causing an unexpected fetch path. However, parts of the finding are not accurate: URI hosts are typically normalized to lowercase (so case-sensitivity is unlikely), and ports don’t affect `URI(...).host` so `http://host:8080` would still pass rather than “silently 403.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26 — same case-sensitivity bug on the referer host; no downcase anywhere

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable the check `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` performs a case-sensitive string comparison. Domain names are case-insensitive, and while Ruby’s `URI(...).host` is typically normalized to lowercase, `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` is compared as-is (no downcasing/normalization in this diff). If an admin configures `embeddable_host` with uppercase/mixed-case (e.g. `Example.COM`), valid requests from `example.com` will be rejected as “invalid referer host”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:19 + loading.html.erb:10 — the loading page is cached 1 minute but reloads itself after 30s, so the reader sits on "Loading Discussion…" for at least a full minute after import completes

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is called unconditionally at the end of the action, including the branch that `render 'loading'` when `topic_id` is not yet available. The loading template auto-reloads the page after 30 seconds (`setTimeout(..., 30000)`), but if `discourse_expires_in` sets a 60s client/proxy cache header (as intended by its name), the browser/proxy can legitimately serve the cached "Loading Discussion..." response on the 30s reload. That makes it possible for users to keep seeing the loading page even after the import completes, until the 60s cache expires. This mismatch is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29,31 — no rescue around open/SimpleRSS.parse or per-item; with retry:false any blip or one bad item silently loses the whole hourly import

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` is performed with no error handling. `open` (network/DNS/timeout) or `SimpleRSS.parse` (malformed feed) can raise, which will abort the entire `poll_feed` run. Additionally, inside `rss.items.each`, operations like `i.content.scrub` can raise if `content` is nil or not a string, which would stop processing remaining items. Since the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, transient failures won’t be retried and the whole hourly import attempt is lost until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — items whose link and id are both non-http are dropped silently with no log

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, each RSS item’s URL is chosen as `url = i.link` and then replaced with `i.id` when the link is blank or not an http(s) URL (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`). However, TopicEmbed.import immediately returns unless the URL matches `^https?\:\/\//`. So if both `i.link` and `i.id` are non-http(s) (or blank), the item results in a no-op (TopicEmbed.import returns nil) and there is no logging or error handling in PollFeed to indicate the item was skipped. This matches the finding: such items are effectively dropped silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — feed_key is dead code, never referenced; the ETag/If-Modified-Since scheme it names is unimplemented, so every poll re-downloads and re-hashes the whole feed

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined but never called anywhere in that file (or anywhere else in this diff). The polling implementation in `poll_feed` directly does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no use of a stored key/Last-Modified/ETag, so there is no conditional-fetch or “modified since” logic implemented despite the `feed_key` name implying such a mechanism. As written, each scheduled run will re-fetch the feed URL in full.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:5 — getElementById('discourse-comments') is not null-checked; appendChild throws on a host page lacking the element

adjudication.rationale: In new file app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is assigned from `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and immediately used as `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no guard. If the embedding script is loaded on a page that does not contain an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:7 — assumes discourseUrl has a trailing slash: "http://forum.example.com" yields "…comembed/best"

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js the iframe URL is built via simple string concatenation: `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?embed_url=" + ...`. If `discourseUrl` is configured as `http://forum.example.com` (no trailing slash), this produces `http://forum.example.comembed/best?...`, which is an invalid path. The code in the diff does not normalize `discourseUrl` (e.g., ensure it ends with `/`) or use a URL-join mechanism, so the assumption is a real correctness issue in this added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1 — discourseUrl/discourseEmbedUrl are declared global but defined nowhere, and the PR ships no docs/route explaining how a host page loads embed.js

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` references `discourseUrl` and `discourseEmbedUrl` without defining them anywhere in this repo change, but the `/* global */` comments indicate they are expected to be provided by the embedding host page (an external integration contract), not by the Rails app itself. The diff also doesn’t have to include docs/routes for how third parties load the asset (Rails asset pipeline serves it), and claiming “no docs” is not a verifiable correctness defect from this diff alone. So this is not a clear bug introduced by the code; it’s an expected configuration requirement for an embed script.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4-5 — topic_id/post_id are NOT NULL with no FK and no ON DELETE; deleting a topic leaves a dangling row that topic_id_for_embed still returns, so #best builds a TopicView for a dead topic and that URL is permanently broken (never falls back to re-import)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` declared `null: false` but with no FK constraints or any `dependent: :destroy`/cleanup shown. `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` blindly returns `pluck(:topic_id).first` without verifying the topic still exists, and `EmbedController#best` then does `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`. Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so a stale/dangling `topic_embeds` row for a deleted topic would both (1) cause `#best` to try to build a view for a missing topic and (2) prevent re-import because the existence check blocks retrieval. This is a concrete correctness hole in the introduced logic if topics/posts can be deleted, and the diff does not add any protection against it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 — embed_url is varchar(255) and carries the UNIQUE index; a >255-char link raises StringDataRightTruncation from create!, aborting the poll. Should be text + UNIQUE on md5(embed_url)

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds.embed_url` as `t.string`, which in Rails maps to `varchar(255)` by default, and then adds a UNIQUE index on that column. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `embed_url` is taken directly from RSS/item links or remote URLs and only checked with a `^https?` regex—no length validation/truncation is applied—then `TopicEmbed.create!` is called. If an embed URL exceeds 255 characters, inserts/updates can fail (e.g., PostgreSQL raises `StringDataRightTruncation`), which would abort the import/polling job. So the finding describes a real correctness risk introduced by the diff (even if the proposed fix is one of several possible approaches).

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3-9 — no index on topic_id or post_id despite both being association keys and topic_id being queried

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `topic_embeds` with `topic_id` and `post_id` but only adds a unique index on `embed_url`. In the diff, the only production query shown (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed`) looks up by `embed_url`, which *is* indexed, and the other lookups are also by `embed_url`. There’s no verifiable production-query path in this diff that depends on indexing `topic_id` or `post_id` for correctness or that demonstrates a clear performance bug; the claim that `topic_id` is queried is not supported by the shown code (aside from tests). This is at most a performance/schema best-practice suggestion, not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 — force: true on a brand-new table can only ever silently DROP an existing topic_embeds, destroying all embed→topic mappings and re-importing every article as a duplicate

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists (typically via `DROP TABLE`) and recreate it, which would silently destroy any existing `topic_embeds` rows (embed_url→topic_id/post_id mappings). While the table is intended to be new, the destructive behavior is real and unnecessary in a migration and could cause data loss if the table exists for any reason (e.g., partially-applied migrations, manual pre-creation, or divergent environments). The additional claim about “re-importing every article as a duplicate” is a plausible consequence but not directly proven by the diff; the data-loss risk itself is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — force: true ADDED to an already-shipped, unrelated migration; on any DB that hasn't run it yet this emits DROP TABLE top_topics. These two are the only force: true in the entire migration set

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table *only if it already exists*; on a DB that “hasn't run it yet” the table typically does not exist, so it will not necessarily emit `DROP TABLE top_topics`. The finding’s claim of a guaranteed drop on any DB that hasn’t run the migration is therefore a misreading. While `force: true` can be risky if the table exists for some reason, that data-loss scenario is conditional and not verifiable as an introduced defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — default: 1 is a magic int hard-wired to the positional ordering of Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html), with no named DB-layer constant and no test asserting cook_methods[:regular] == 1; reordering silently reinterprets every row

adjudication.rationale: The migration sets `cook_method` default to integer `1`, while the model defines `cook_methods` via `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`. In this codebase pattern, `Enum`-backed integer columns commonly use numeric defaults (e.g., `Post.types` already exists and likely maps `:regular` to `1`), and migrations cannot directly depend on model constants reliably. The finding describes a general maintainability risk inherent to any positional integer-enum (reordering symbols would change meaning), but the diff does not show any actual mismatch, breakage, or imminent reordering; it’s not a concrete defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:321 — before_save re-derives cooked through the raw_html branch on every save, giving cooked two divergent producers (this callback and post_creator.rb:105 `cooked ||=`) with no owner for the raw_html case

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, plus passes/assigns `cook_method` via `PostCreator`. There is no shown `before_save` callback in `app/models/post.rb` (certainly not at “:321” in this diff) and nothing here indicates cooked is re-derived “on every save” via a callback. The mention of `post_creator.rb:105 cooked ||= ...` is also not verifiable from this diff (the only shown change in `post_creator.rb` is setting `post.cook_method`). Therefore the finding relies on code/line numbers not present in the diff and is not a verifiable problem introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:456 — the Schema Information annotation was not regenerated; it omits the new cook_method column

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `cook_method` column via a migration and updates `app/models/post.rb` logic, but it does not show any `Schema Information` comment block in `post.rb` (or any change to such an annotation). Without the annotation being present in the shown file content, it’s not verifiable from this diff that it exists and is now stale/omits the column. This is therefore speculative and not a demonstrable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — the user-facing --category/-c option and its lookup are deleted; existing scripted invocations now fail with a Thor unknown-option error. Unrelated to embed URL handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and also deletes all code that reads `options[:category]`, looks up the Category, and passes it to `PostCreator`. With Thor, invoking the task with an undeclared option (e.g., `--category`/`-c` used by existing scripts) will raise an unknown-option error. This is a concrete backward-incompatible change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — drops created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) for the opening post while line 164 still preserves it for replies, so imported topics show an opening post newer than its own comments

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import code previously created the opening post via `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)`. The diff removes that and replaces it with `post = TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` do not pass any `created_at` option into `PostCreator` (they only pass `title`, `raw`, `skip_validations`, `cook_method`). Therefore the opening post will default to “now”, while the code that creates replies in the subsequent loop is unchanged by this diff and (per the finding) still uses the Disqus-provided timestamps. This mismatch can make the topic’s first post appear newer than its own replies/comments, which is a correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 — converts a deterministic offline XML import into one live HTTP fetch per thread with no rescue; a single dead link aborts the run mid-way, leaving a partially imported forum

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the previous implementation created a topic/post directly from the parsed Disqus XML data (PostCreator with a permalink) and did not perform any network access per thread. The diff replaces that with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (TopicEmbed model) with no exception handling. If any thread link is unreachable/raises (e.g., OpenURI::HTTPError, SocketError, Timeout), the Thor task will raise and abort mid-loop, after potentially having already imported earlier threads, leaving a partial import state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile:206-211 — the two new gems land only in Gemfile_rails4.lock; the dual-boot RAILS3 path (Gemfile:5-11, 23-27) resolves against Gemfile.lock, which this diff never touches

In a dual-lockfile setup (implied by the presence of `Gemfile_rails4.lock`), changing the shared `Gemfile` without updating the other lockfile will leave the non-Rails4/baseline bundle state inconsistent/out-of-date and can break installs/tests for that path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:18,24 — both "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" are vacuous: feed_polling_enabled? is unstubbed and defaults false, so the && short-circuits and they pass even if the guards are deleted

In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb, the "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples stub only the url/username to nil but do not stub feed_polling_enabled?. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8 — "is 404 without an embed_url" never reaches params.require (ensure_embeddable raises first on the default blank embeddable_host); the name is also wrong — Rails 4.0 maps ParameterMissing to 400, not 404

The diff adds `embeddable_host: ''` in `site_settings.yml`, so by default it’s blank, meaning `get :best` (with no params) will fail in the before_filter and never reach `params.require(:embed_url)`. Thus the spec example labeled "is 404 without an embed_url" is not actually exercising the missing-parameter path. Also, the example name claims 404 but the spec only asserts `should_not be_success`, and in Rails 4 `ActionController::ParameterMissing` typically maps to 400 (not 404) if it were reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — asserts TopicRetriever.expects(:new) while the controller does Jobs.enqueue; passes only because queue_jobs is false in test, so the actual async contract, the embed_url payload and no_throttle are all uncovered

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:19 — the only URL-validation test is "invalid url"; no coverage of import_remote, topic_id_for_embed, the ^ anchor bypass, javascript:/data:/file:, the 255-char limit, or any absolutize_urls edge case

adjudication_records.issue_text: The dominant theme: the PR is titled "enhance … validation," but its net effect on validation is **subtractive** — `skip_validations` on both create and revise paths, plus a total sanitization bypass (`post.rb:133`) feeding attacker-controlled HTML from an RSS feed straight into `cooked`. The `poll_feed.rb:35` → `topic_embed.rb:13` → `best.html.erb:19` chain is the one I'd block on.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces an explicit sanitization/rendering bypass for imported content: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `skip_validations: true` and `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In `Post#cook`, `raw_html` returns `raw` directly, skipping the normal cooking pipeline (which is where HTML is typically normalized/sanitized). The scheduled `Jobs::PollFeed` path feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` from a remote RSS/Atom feed into `TopicEmbed.import`, and the embed UI renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`. `scrub` only addresses encoding/invalid bytes, not XSS. So attacker-controlled HTML from the feed (or `import_remote` via `open(url).read` + Readability) can be stored and served as-is, which is a verifiable security defect introduced by this diff. The validation bypass (`skip_validations` on create and revise, and `PostRevisor` now honoring it via `save(validate: ...)`) is also real and part of that chain.
